name: video-chapters
title: A Film, in Chapters
claim: One agent watches NASA's 1969 Apollo 11 film a minute at a time, sound included, writes its chapters with a keyframe each, survives a kill mid-film, and pays for each minute once.

oneOf.why: The lead (openai/gpt-6-luna), and the eyes too when it is the only key (openai/gpt-6-sol, which takes frames, not video).
The eyes (google/gemini-3.8-flash, which takes a video window with its sound), and the lead too when it is the only key.
The lead and the eyes (anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5, which takes frames) when it is the only key.
An OpenAI-compatible gateway that serves the models under their public ids, instead of provider keys.
oneOf.where: your gateway's base URL, ending in /v1

keys.why: A model provider's key for --live (the run names every model by provider and public id).

programs.why: The agent's code cuts the film's windows and keyframes with it.
The agent's code reads the film's length with it.

kills.why: Inside the evidence sink, at the second window's filing: the eyes have answered it and the answer is kept, and the look is not yet filed. A fresh process runs the agent's script again: the first window comes back kept, the second from its kept answer, nothing paid twice.

input.shape: examples/video-chapters/job.ts, Input: the film (a file in the workspace), the seconds to read from and to, the seconds of film in one look
input.default: NASA's film whole, in windows of 60 s (what --live reads); a run on fakes reads the committed clip (clip/clip.json) in windows of 8 s, with no network
